newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares close at record after touching 605.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares close at record after touching 605.

text.p: Dutch shares rose to their fourth consecutive record closing high, boosted by Wall Street's overnight strength and firmer bonds, as well as short covering ahead of Friday's options market expirations.
Dealers said news on Wednesday that the U.S. was leaving its monetary policy unchanged gave another boost to the market as did the steady trend in the dollar.

The AEX index of 25 leading Dutch shares closed 2.89 points or 0.48 percent higher at a record 604.91, settling above the 600 level which it crossed for the first time on Wednesday but just below the 605.24 high it touched during Thursday.

Dealers said a brisk two-way trade developed on Thursday with opinions split over the direction of shares in the near term. Some are buying on the view that fundamentals for stable interest rates remain in place while others believe that the market could be due for a consolidation to around 590 as Wall Street's bull run looks ripe for a correction.

The past few sessions in Amsterdam have been dominated by options-related business with traders reporting a big-build up of open interest in November 600 calls. They say this reflects mainly retail buying of calls which began a few weeks ago when the AEX was trading around the 580 level.

"A lot of market makers have the opposite view and they're sitting on positions where they could get hurt if that happens, so you can expect them to try again to get the index back below the 600 level tomorrow," said one trader.

"The only thing that the market makers really need is a weaker Dow Jones close tonight and that could be enough to tip the AEX lower tomorrow," he said. In late Amsterdam trading Wall Street was showing a six point decline, opening lower after eight days on the upside.
But others believe the market makers will have to grin and bear it as the AEX looks stable above 600 for the moment.
